# Independent audit: proper deepest heredity and the mixed parity budget

Audited source:
`candidate abd48c3f5afc0115`,
Sections 1--7. Verdict: PASS, without adding a differentiability, regular-
cap or singleton-face hypothesis. No correction found.

## 1. Actual cap equality and inherited status

At any positive-depth deepest mark the own point is interior, by the
finite continuous-normal support-plane argument and boundary-zero energy.
At an atomic deepest mark, a single own direction omitting positive mass,
combined with a large atomic minimizing tilt, would contradict the depth.
Thus every own buffered trace is full. At a strict-base-gap deepest mark,
tilts have compact representatives; an active cap is attained and its
own trace must be proper by the whole-fiber capture lemma.

For the mark formed from deepest inputs at r in J, the active cap's own
properness makes the tail strictly decreasing locally at its threshold.
Continuity and monotonicity then make that threshold the EXACT right
upper quantile c_Q, even if other fiber sections are supporting. Every
input deepest mark obeys the same quantile inequality. Their weighted
sum and concavity of f force equality in both places, including equality
of every input cap threshold. There is no assumed derivative here.

Positivity and affine ell make equality in the weighted geometric mean
force F_j/ell_j constant, while equality in joint energy concavity gives
marked homothety of the WHOLE actual fibers and rules out an enlarged
target fiber. The multilateral version follows by positive grouping and
repeated two-input equality; all intermediate real fibers are legitimate
fibers of the canonical hull. Hence K_j-y_j=ell_j K_* and f_j/ell_j is
common. The SAME actual cap therefore has the identical normalized
own trace in every input and target. It is proper at r, excluding every
atomic input. This proves the asserted heredity with no shape regularity.

The strict epsilon>0 premise is essential and correctly retained.

## 2. Closed minors, atomic witnesses and boundary atoms

The strict atomic base-depth region is convex: the finite measure has
finitely many possible halfspace masses, so its strict Q-superlevel is
one ordinary nonstrict superlevel above Q. Interpolating actual deepest
marks then proves J=P intersect conv(J).

Every chosen mass-Q atomic cap excludes all of J strictly. Expanding
its threshold only preserves this exclusion. Maximal threshold witnesses
lie in A, with equality in their own cap and strict inequality in all
others. The compressed caps retain mass exactly Q because each contains
an atomic-depth-Q witness.

A same-parity pair of atomic witnesses has an integer deepest midpoint.
All compressed caps exclude this midpoint strictly, so their cover of A
would place it in J. Heredity forbids its atomic inputs. The same argument
with a witness and any point of J excludes shared parities with J. Thus
m+k(J)<=k(I) is exact. No boundary point has been moved from a closed cap
to its complement by convention.

The two-interval sharp-count example checks independently: Sigma=7/48,
the two squared physical center shifts are 1/4 and 1/16, and both unique
maxima are Q=1. The geometric normalization and compensating epsilon
factor leave those shifts unchanged. Its safe depth 2/5 correctly prevents
it from being mistaken for a bad minimum.

## 3. Two additional scoped consequences

First A=I outside J is ALSO a closed minor of P. Any lattice point in
conv(A) lies in I by buffered convexity and lattice completeness. If it
lay in J, its positive anchored representation by A would violate the
proved heredity. Thus A=P intersect conv(A). This does not imply that
conv(A) or conv(J) is an exposed face, or that their entire parity sets
are disjoint. Only the selected witness parities have that latter property.

Second, assume the strict proper-minor quotas with total occupied budget
k=k(P), and suppose A and J are nonempty. The compressed caps give

    V(A)<=mQ,

while J is a proper closed minor and therefore

    V(J)<k(J)M/k.

Consequently the actual mass outside the deepest stratum satisfies

    V(P outside I)>M[1-k(J)/k-m beta].

In particular I cannot equal P when beta<1/k and A is nonempty: the
mixed parity bound makes the right side strictly positive. Under the
bad target beta<Gamma_d/k this condition is automatic. This is an exact
outside-mass constraint, not payment for that mass by any continuous cap.
If J were empty, the separate all-atomic hinge theorem already excludes
a bad minimum. Neither statement erases the remaining mixed responses.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
